transferable_lessons: For counting questions about fast, frequently repeated, sub-second visual actions (e.g. drinking/eating/attack animations in game footage), a single coarse fps sample (1fps) over a long span is insufficient; the answer requires either much higher uniform fps across the entire span or an exhaustive sliding-window scan, not just zooming into a handful of coarse-pass candidates.

When text search (semantic_search + SQL keyword search) returns zero hits for the target action across the entire clue window, treat that as a signal the DB captioning pipeline missed a high-frequency visual event -- don't assume the low count from a quick visual sub-agent pass is complete; budget for denser re-sampling given the mismatch between the 13x reference count and rapid combat pacing.
Never scan a combined multi-hundred-second span with a single clip_qa call for a counting question (rollout 2's mistake); split per clue window (or smaller) to preserve sampling density per call.

For counting tasks with a plausible high true count, treat a low count from one pass as a lower bound and re-verify with an independent denser sampling pass or multiple overlapping windows before submitting.
